_comment: The in-game Compendium (scenes/ui/CompendiumScreen.gd). Topics are grouped by section. Text is BBCode. Placeholders pull live values so the Compendium stays true when you retune: {pct:file:path} -> percent, {num:file:path} -> number, {x:file:path} -> x-multiplier (file = a data file name, path = dot path inside it), and {list:name} inserts a generated block (classes, attributes, formulas, status_effects, elite_affixes, omens, boons, ranks, challenges, enchants, damage_types).

topics.title: Getting started
topics.text:
[b]You are a new member of the Adventurer Guild.[/b] Your goal: become the Guild's top adventurer - #1 on the Guild Ledger and its crowned Champion.

[b]The loop[/b]
• In town, prepare: gear (Shop, Blacksmith, Enchanter), potions (Alchemist), work (Guild bounties, shop commissions), companions (Tavern).
• Set out on an [b]expedition[/b]: pick a location and starting floor, optionally take Omens, then fight floor by floor. Each floor is 5 waves and a boss.
• After each won wave choose [b]Press On[/b] (keep your Momentum, loot is banked) or [b]Take a Breather[/b] (collect the loot, rest).
• Come home: time passes, the world moves on, rivals climb the Ledger.

[b]Where to look[/b]
• [b]Journal[/b] (town): everything you're working on.
• [b]Guild → Ledger[/b]: the standings.
• [b]Combos[/b] and [b]Bestiary[/b] (town): what your party can do and what you've learned about enemies.

topics.title: Attributes
Derived stats and damage
topics.text: {list:formulas}

topics.title: Classes
Levels and talents
topics.text:
Winning waves gives XP (more for higher-level enemies and deeper floors). Each level costs a little more than the last: {num:progression:xp.base} + {num:progression:xp.per_level} x (level-1) + {num:progression:xp.per_level_sq} x (level-1)² XP.

Levels give attribute points and talent points. Talents (town → Talents) raise stats, unlock skills and, at the end of each branch, an [b]ultimate[/b].

topics.title: Forks, mutations and attribute passives
topics.text:
Every talent branch has three [b]forks[/b] - pick one of two, and the other locks until you respec:

• [b]Tier 3 - skill mutation:[/b] change how the branch's skill works. Hit every foe instead of one, strike once much harder, add a status, knock them further back, or gain something yourself when you use it.
• [b]Tier 4 - passive:[/b] deepen the branch's style, or bend it toward another (offence or defence, yourself or the party).
• [b]Tier 5 - ultimate mutation:[/b] the same choice for your ultimate.

Mutated skills show [i]Mutated: <name>[/i] in battle. A respec refunds everything for a fee that rises with your level.

[b]Attribute passives[/b] switch on while an attribute - counting your gear, not buffs - is at or above a threshold. Check your progress on the Talents screen.
{list:thresholds}

topics.title: Turns and actions
topics.text:
Battles are turn-based. The [b]turn order[/b] (under the dungeon banner) shows who acts next; "|" marks the next round, which is re-rolled. Agility decides who goes first.

On your turn: one [b]main action[/b] (Attack, Defend, a Skill) and, separately, one [b]Item[/b].
• [b]Attack[/b]: a basic hit that also restores some MP and SP.
• [b]Defend[/b]: halves the damage you take until your next turn.
• [b]Skills[/b]: cost MP (magic) or SP (physical) and may have a cooldown. Buffs and debuffs last a few turns.

Some skills push enemies back in the turn order or pull an ally forward.

topics.title: Intents and Perfect Guard
topics.text:
Every enemy shows its [b]next action[/b] on its panel ("Fireball → Mira", "Howl → everyone"), and does what it showed.

[b]Charge-ups:[/b] bosses (at HP thresholds) and sometimes regular enemies ({pct:combat:intents.regular_charge_chance} of strong skills) spend a turn winding up. The charged strike hits {x:combat:intents.charge_power_mult}. Break the enemy to cancel it, or brace.

[b]Perfect Guard:[/b] Defend while an enemy's shown intent targets you (or something is charging). You take only {pct:combat:guard.damage_mult} of the already-halved damage, gain no Break pips, the attacker gains {num:combat:guard.attacker_pips} Break pip, and a charged strike is countered. The Defend button reads "⛨ Perfect Guard" when it applies.

Guarding costs your attack, so save it for the big or charged hits.

topics.title: Weaknesses and Break
topics.text:
Every creature has damage types and elements it's [b]weak to[/b] (from its race and armor). Hitting a weakness deals the affinity bonus plus another {pct:combat:weakness_bonus}.

{list:damage_types}

[b]Break:[/b] each weakness hit fills a Break pip (a hit that also triggers a combo fills one more). When the pips are full the target is [b]Broken[/b]: it loses its next turn, takes +{pct:combat:break.broken_damage_bonus} damage until then, and loses any charge or shield. Regular enemies need {num:combat:break.regular_hits} hits, elites {num:combat:break.elite_hits}, bosses {num:combat:break.boss_hits}; each Break raises it by {num:combat:break.growth_per_break}.

[b]Heroes have Break pips too[/b] ({num:combat:break.hero_hits} hits): enemies hitting your weaknesses can Break you.

[b]Hidden weaknesses:[/b] enemy weaknesses show ??? until you find them - a weakness hit reveals it, a Break studies the race, and Inspect studies an enemy when your party has a scholar. The Bestiary keeps what you've learned.

topics.title: Combos, Link and Unison
topics.text:
[b]Combos:[/b] one skill sets up a status (Freeze, Bleed, Soaked, Marked...), another pays it off for bonus damage. The [b]Combos[/b] screen lists the ones your party can do.

[b]Link gauge[/b] (under your panel): fills from hits (shared by the party), combos (+{num:combat:link.gain_combo}) and Breaks (+{num:combat:break.link_gain}).
• [b]Ultimates[/b] cost {num:combat:link.ultimate_cost} Link.
• [b]Unison Strike[/b] spends a full gauge: every standing hero strikes one enemy together ({x:combat:link.unison_mult}).
• [b]Duo techs[/b] ({num:bonds:link_cost} Link) unlock when you bond with a companion: you strike together and they act next.

topics.title: Status effects
topics.text: {list:status_effects}

topics.title: Elites and bosses
Momentum, Press On and Breathers
topics.text:
After each won wave:
• [b]Press On[/b]: Momentum +1 - you deal +5% damage per level, but don't rest, and the wave's loot is [b]banked[/b] (lost if you fall).
• [b]Take a Breather[/b]: collect everything banked plus this wave, with +10% per Momentum level (up to +50%). You rest; Momentum resets.

[b]Wave challenges:[/b] {pct:challenges:chance} of waves (every boss wave) offer an optional goal shown under the turn order. Meet it and win to bank bonus gold, materials and maybe gear.

{list:challenges}

[b]Defeat:[/b] the Guild carries you home - a gold fee, an injury, and some equipped gear goes to the Guild's Lost & Found, where you can buy it back for a while.

topics.title: Omens and boons
Encounters and rivals
topics.text:
Other Guild adventurers are out there too, and you'll meet them:
• [b]Helpers[/b] - friends who fight beside you.
• [b]The wounded[/b] - share a potion (they'll remember) or leave them.
• [b]Thieves[/b] - a rival takes part of your banked loot; confront them or let it go.
• [b]Saboteurs[/b] - someone who dislikes you joins the enemy mid-wave or ambushes you after it.
• [b]Nemesis[/b] - a rival at rivalry {num:encounters:types.nemesis.min_rivalry}, or anyone who beat you in an ambush, returns stronger with a grudge. Beat them for their signature item.

[b]Rumours[/b] (Tavern) point to a named Elite on a floor, or a cache past a floor's boss - follow one up for a bonus.

topics.title: Gear, Blacksmith and Enchanter
topics.text:
[b]Rarity[/b]: Common, Uncommon, Magic, Rare, Epic, Legendary - higher rarities have more bonuses and better base stats. Enemies sometimes drop what they wear; bosses always drop a piece.

[b]Blacksmith[/b]: upgrade gear (+8% damage/armor per level). Higher levels can fail (Tempered: +5% next try); from +7 a failure drops a level. Reinforce to pay more for better odds. Weapons, mail and plate use ore; cloth armor uses cloth, leather armor uses hide. Salvage unwanted gear for materials.

[b]Enchanter[/b]: raise an item one rarity tier (up to {list:enchant_cap}) and add an enchantment - the material decides the effect. It can fail (materials lost, item unharmed; Attuned +{pct:enchanting:fail_bonus} next try).

{list:enchants}

topics.title: Town services
topics.text:
• [b]Shop[/b]: potions and gear. Selling gear pays {pct:shop:sell_fraction.equipment} of its value.
• [b]Alchemist[/b]: craft potions, tonics, bombs and combo set-up items from materials. Learn recipes by reaching floors, ranks, buying them, or standing with the Alchemist.
• [b]Inn[/b]: rest to pass days.
• [b]Commissions[/b]: shops ask for materials. Deliveries build standing (Known, Valued, Partner): discounts, better odds and special recipes.
• [b]Bestiary[/b]: the enemy weaknesses you've found.
• [b]Journal[/b]: your open objectives.
• [b]Compendium[/b]: this book.

topics.title: The Guild and ranks
topics.text:
[b]Bounties[/b]: accept work from the Guild board (defeat, deliver, clear, streak). Finish within the deadline for gold, materials and [b]Guild points[/b]; missing one costs points and a demerit.

[b]Ranks[/b]: earn the next rank's Guild points, then pass its promotion trial. Higher ranks unlock deeper floors, bigger parties and better rewards.

{list:ranks}

The [b]Infirmary[/b] treats injuries; [b]Lost Gear[/b] sells back what you lost when defeated.

topics.title: Companions and bonds
topics.text:
The [b]Tavern[/b] is where the Guild's adventurers rest. Chat, buy a drink or give a gift to raise [b]rapport[/b]; friends can join your party (party size depends on your rank) and take a share of the loot.

Everyone has traits that shape how they act - and how they react to [b]your choices[/b] (pressing on, Omens, helping the wounded...).

[b]Bonds[/b]: at rapport 25 / 50 / 75 a companion opens up (Acquainted, Trusted, Bonded) in a short scene at the Tavern. Bonded companions unlock a duo tech.

topics.title: Personalities
topics.text:
Every adventurer has a [b]personality[/b] on top of their traits:
• an [b]archetype[/b] - how they present and how they grow,
• a [b]drive[/b] - what they want (revealed as you get to know them),
• a [b]flaw[/b] - what can break them (only friends know),
• [b]quirks[/b] - small things that make them memorable.

Archetypes have [b]arcs[/b]: as your rapport grows they change - the prickly warm up, the shy speak up, rivals become friends. Their drives play out in the world: an avenger keeps returning to where their sibling died.

[b]You[/b] have a reputation too: your choices (pressing on, helping the wounded, confronting thieves, taking Omens...) shape how the Guild sees you. Check the Journal.

{list:archetypes}

topics.title: Memories and reputation
topics.text:
Adventurers [b]remember[/b] what others did - to them, and to people they care about. Saving someone, helping, fighting side by side and gifts are remembered fondly; leaving someone to die, robbing, ambushing or betraying them are not.

• Most memories [b]fade[/b] over weeks; the deepest (a loved one killed, a death avenged) never do.
• People [b]gossip[/b] - mostly with their friends - so what you do spreads, a little weaker each time it is retold.
• Someone with a [color=#ff9f6b]grudge[/color] won't join your party, and may turn up to ambush you on an expedition.
• Someone you [color=#7bd389]saved[/color] owes you: when you fall, they may carry you home - no fee, no lost gear.
• A rival you keep beating studies you: after {num:social:memory.nemesis_learns_after} losses they come back armored against your weapon.

At the Tavern you only see a hint of how someone remembers you until your rapport reaches {num:social:memory.full_view_rapport}; then they tell you plainly. [b]You[/b] remember too - the Journal lists the people who left a mark on you.

topics.title: Relationships
topics.text:
Adventurers have opinions of [b]each other[/b], not just of you. Two who meet in town grow closer or apart depending on their traits (the kind get on, the cruel grate); shared jobs, rescues, promotions and the race up the Ledger all leave their mark.

• [color=#7bd389]Friends[/color] ({num:social:relations.thresholds.friends}+) often take jobs together - together they do better, and one may drag the other out alive when things go wrong.
• [color=#ffd166]Sworn companions[/color] ({num:social:relations.thresholds.sworn}+) almost always go together.
• [color=#ff9f6b]Rivals[/color] ({num:social:relations.thresholds.rivals} or lower) and [color=#ff6b6b]feuds[/color] ({num:social:relations.thresholds.feud} or lower) sour the Guild.

[b]You are part of the web:[/b] when you win someone over, their friends warm to you a little - and their rivals cool. People also gossip mostly with their friends, so what you do travels along these bonds. The Tavern shows who is close to whom.

topics.title: Companies, love and loss
topics.text:
The Guild's adventurers live their own stories.

[b]Companies.[/b] Sworn companions found a named company and take jobs together. A death, a retirement or a quarrel can break one up.

[b]Invitations.[/b] A small company with a friend of yours may invite you along. Accept at the Tavern and they fight beside you on your next expedition, then go back to their own work - and remember the job.

[b]Romance.[/b] Sworn companions may fall for each other. A bad enough falling-out ends it.

[b]Grief.[/b] When someone dies, their friends grieve for a few weeks and take fewer jobs. Then, depending on who they are, they [color=#ff9f6b]swear vengeance[/color] (on the boss that killed their friend, or on the person who did), [color=#9fb4ff]leave the Guild[/color], [color=gray]go cold[/color], or carry on. Kill the boss an avenger is after and they will never forget it.

[b]Feuds.[/b] Bitter enemies may come to blows - and if one of them is cruel, it can end in a death. The Guild punishes killers with demerits and a lower rank, and the dead have friends.

[b]Careers.[/b] Nobody adventures forever: after a few years veterans start to retire, and new faces sign up.

[b]Jealousy.[/b] Some devotion turns possessive. If someone who adores you seems uneasy about who else you spend time with, keep an eye on the people you are close to.

topics.title: Temperament
topics.text:
An adventurer's [b]traits[/b] are not just labels - they act on them.

• [b]In town[/b], every day: the Kind tend the injured (you too, if they like you), the Greedy pick pockets (yours too, if they don't), the Scholarly teach, the Devout hold vigils for the dead, the Cheerful throw parties, the Cruel pick on the weak - and the decent stand up to them - the Honorable make bitter rivals talk it out, the Loyal set gossips straight, the Ambitious challenge whoever is just above them on the Ledger. Hear it all as [i]Tavern talk[/i] in the Rumours at the Tavern.
• [b]In battle[/b], companions fight like themselves: the Cowardly may freeze when badly hurt, the Loyal heal you first, the Kind heal anyone, the Cautious guard, the Reckless never do, the Cruel finish off the weakest.
• [b]Over time[/b], people change: a coward who drags a friend out of the depths may find their nerve; the reckless learn after a near-death or two; the kind can be wronged once too often; the bullied may pass it on.
• Their traits colour what they [b]say[/b], too.

topics.title: The living world
topics.text:
Time moves in days: expeditions take days (travel + floors), resting at the Inn passes them too. A year is 4 seasons of 4 weeks.

Every day the world moves on without you: adventurers take jobs, climb ranks, get injured, retire or die; rivals out-rank you if you idle; world events change locations for a while; the shop restocks weekly. The town news reports it all.

topics.title: The Ledger and the Crowning
topics.text:
The [b]Guild Ledger[/b] ranks you and every adventurer by [b]renown[/b]: rank x{num:ledger:weights.per_rank}, Guild points x{num:ledger:weights.per_point}, deepest floor cleared x{num:ledger:weights.per_floor}, bosses slain x{num:ledger:weights.per_boss}, level x{num:ledger:weights.per_level}, World Firsts x{num:ledger:weights.per_first}, crowns x{num:ledger:weights.per_crown}.

[b]The Crowning[/b]: at the turn of each year the Ledger's #1 is crowned Champion. If it's you, the Guild pays you and your renown grows; if it's someone else, they hold the title until overtaken.

Your goal: S-rank, #1 on the Ledger, and the crown.
